headline: High-risk shared-filesystem coding agent can inject, leak, and corrupt data when paired with a non-networked data engine; compliance risk is low but interaction is underdocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has shared-state via filesystem and can write files; Agent B is a data-engineering system with no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if B consumes A-produced files or outputs. The pairwise interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty does not justify lowering severity.
conditions: IF Agent B reads files or SQL/text produced by Agent A as trusted input
IF both agents operate in the same workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Add provenance tags to all handoff files
Require explicit allowlist parsing for B inputs
Review any A-generated text before B consumes it

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read and write the user filesystem and handle secrets; Agent B has no documented file access or egress, so a direct leak path is not shown. The main risk is shared workspace exposure from A, while B appears non-networked. Because the pairwise data flow is undocumented, this stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared cwd
IF Agent B is later extended to read from that workspace
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared directory
Mount a read-only workspace for B
Rotate any exposed tokens after the run
Use separate OS users for the two agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Agent B is a data-engineering system likely to touch shared datasets or repositories, but its write surfaces are not documented. The overlap is therefore plausible but uncertain, and uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low because A's defaults are already mutable.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or dataset
IF Agent B is configured with any mutable storage connector
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Assign separate branches or tables
Disable concurrent runs on the same target
Snapshot the workspace before either agent writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code or files that Agent B may ingest as authoritative data, and B's data-engineering role suggests downstream transformation or action. No verification or review step is documented between them, so an A error can cascade into B outputs. The interaction is inferred, but the default mutable workflow makes medium appropriate.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes artifacts produced by Agent A without validation
IF A-generated schemas, SQL, or configs are deployed downstream
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on all handoffs
Diff A outputs against a known-good template
Block direct execution of A-generated code

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles source code and files in cwd, while Agent B has no documented data classes or residency constraints. There is no evidence of a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a generic compliance gap exists. Because the other agent is not documented as processing regulated data, the risk remains low and one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF Agent B is used in a jurisdiction or policy regime requiring retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings before use
Purge shared artifacts after completion
Review vendor/data-processing terms
